description: Pareto distribution survival function (x_m/x)^alpha (shape alpha, scale x_m)

tolerance.reason: x, alpha and x_m are exact doubles and x_m is a power of two. The condition number in t = alpha log(x/x_m) is t itself, 708.4 at the last normal result, so rounding t once costs up to 7.9e-14 there (as for weibull_sf); where x_m/x is a normal double, pow(x_m/x, alpha) costs only alpha ulps (at most 100, 1.1e-14) plus one. Results below 2.2e-308 are judged relative to that number (conventions)

grid: the pareto_cdf grid: shape alpha in {2^-5, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3.5, 10, 100} x scale x_m = 2^m for m in {-500, -10, 0, 10, 500} x x = u x_m for u in {1, 1 + 2^-52, 1 + 1e-15, 1 + 1e-10, 1 + 1e-5, 1.001, 1.1, 1.5, 2, 5, 10, 100, 1e5, 1e10, 1e20, 1e50, 1e100, 1e200, 1e300, 1.1 2^1030, 1.1 2^1060, 2^1100, 2^1500}, kept where x is normal and finite (so x/x_m = u exactly as a real number), plus x = x_m (1 - 2^-53), x_m/2, 0 and -x_m below the support; Q is 1 for x < x_m, subnormal from about t = 708.40 and 0 above about t = 745.13 with t = alpha log(x/x_m)
